hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up on $2 \times [10 - (1 + 2 \times 2)]$. Inside: $2 \times 2 = 4$, then $1 + 4 = 5$, then $10 - 5 = 5$, then $2 \times 5 = 10$. The big problem uses exactly that order.
Work from the innermost grouping outward. Inside each grouping, remember that multiplication is done before addition.
Inside the parentheses, do $2 \times 3 = 6$ first and then $4 + 6 = 10$. The brackets now hold $20 - 10$, and the result is multiplied by $3$.

explanation: Start inside the parentheses $(4 + 2 \times 3)$. Multiplication comes before addition, so $2 \times 3 = 6$ and then $4 + 6 = 10$.
Now the brackets read $20 - 10$, which equals $10$.
Finally multiply by the number in front of the brackets: $3 \times 10 = 30$.
The whole expression has a value of $30$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The classic wrong answer is $6$: it comes from adding $4 + 2 = 6$ first, then $6 \times 3 = 18$, then $20 - 18 = 2$ and $3 \times 2 = 6$.
The problem is that left-to-right does not win inside parentheses — multiplication still goes before addition.
Escape it by circling $2 \times 3$ before you touch the $4$, so the multiplication is finished first every time.
